topic: What antenna design considerations optimize ground station visibility during short service windows in LEO constellations?
response: Optimizing ground station visibility in LEO requires antenna designs that maximize signal reception within short service windows. This involves selecting high gain antennas with narrow beamwidths to minimize interference from other signals and maximizing line-of-sight (LOS) to the satellite.  Specific standards like TR 38.821 are essential for detailed design.
reference_context: The paper details a new paradigm for LEO communication systems, focusing on improving observability for radio astronomy (RAS). This involves addressing data transport issues and service degradation caused by RFI (Radio Frequency Interference) from LEO satellites. Ground telescopes may be affected by the increased number of LEO satellites in space.
